Listen to this article Share The Correspondents Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Abia State, is set to train over 50 journalists and media practitioners ahead of the 2027 general elections as part of activities marking its 2026 Press Week. The three-day programme, scheduled to hold from Wednesday, November 4 to Friday, November 6, 2026, at Bishop Anthony Nwedo Pastoral Centre, BCA Road, Umuahia, will feature a two-day professional retreat and a grand finale designed to strengthen the capacity of journalists for credible, ethical and responsible election reporting. Governor Alex Otti is the special guest at the grand finale, while Okey Kanu, Commissioner for Information, will declare the retreat open on Wednesday. The retreat with the theme: “The Future of Journalism in an Era of Disinformation: Preparing Abia Media Practitioners for Democracy and the 2027 Polls,” is expected to equip participants with essential professional skills and digital tools to navigate the increasingly complex media landscape, particularly in the face of rising misinformation, disinformation, deepfakes and the misuse of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Participants will be exposed to critical areas of contemporary journalism, including the responsible application of AI in news reporting, fact-checking and verification of political claims, ethical election coverage, media safety, hate speech, inflammatory political communication and the role of the media in promoting peaceful, credible and issue-based elections. The retreat is expected to feature distinguished resource persons, including Uchenna Agu, a Professor and Resident Electoral Commissioner in Abia State; Wilfred Afolabi, Abia State Commissioner of Police, and Stella Okunna, the first female Professor of Mass Communication in Nigeria. Others include Ralph Egbu, veteran journalist and former Secretary to Abia State Government; Chimezie Okwuonu, Chief Medical Director, Abia Specialist Hospital and Chibueze Ukaegbu, a digital expert. The Correspondents Chapel in a statement, jointly signed by Steve Oko, Chairman; Henrietta Ashikodi, Secretary; Peter Okore, Planning Committee Chairman and Leonard Okachie, Secretary, Planning Committee, said a keynote speech would be delivered by Christopher Okoro, a Professor and Rector Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic Aba. According to the statement, Uwaoma Uche, Professor and Deputy Vice Chancellor of Gregory University, Uturu, will chair the grand finale of the event, which will feature a political debate by National Assembly candidates from various political parties on November 6. The release said that the programme was conceived in response to the growing demands of election reporting in an era where digital manipulation and the proliferation of false information pose serious threats to democratic processes. It noted that credible elections and functional democracy depend substantially on an informed electorate, accurate information and a professionally equipped media capable of holding political actors accountable. The chapel said that it is determined to ensure that journalists in Abia State are adequately prepared to confront the challenges of the 2027 elections through continuous training, professional development and strict adherence to ethical standards. According to the release, the political debate cum manifesto presentation by the National Assembly candidates is to provide them an opportunity to present their programmes and policy proposals to the electorate through the chapel’s media platforms. The release said that the initiative was designed to promote political neutrality, equal media access and issue-based engagement while empowering voters with the information required to make informed electoral choices. It further said that the event would also feature the presentation of awards to distinguished Nigerians in recognition of their contributions to leadership, public service and sports. The honourees include David Umahi, Minister of Works, Nnenna Oti, the immediate past Vice Chancellor of Federal University of Science and Technology, Owerri (FUTO) and Samuel Chukwueze of the Super Eagles. According to the release, the Press Week will underscore the critical role of journalism in democratic development, particularly as the country approaches another electoral cycle, while reaffirming the chapel’s commitment to credible reporting, accountability and peaceful political participation.
